transcribed: read from the Cadetprep Excel sheet by extract-cadetprep.ts (sheet row = n); key and solution are the source's, kept as evidence

questions.stem: From a standard deck, what is the probability of drawing a card greater than \(8\) (considering Jack=\(11\), Queen=\(12\), King=\(13\), Ace=\(14\))?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Cards greater than 8: 9, 10, J, Q, K, A
Step 2: Number of such cards per suit = \(6\)
Step 3: Total such cards = \(6 \times 4 = 24\)
Step 4: Probability = \(\frac{24}{52} = \frac{6}{13}\)

questions.stem: From two cards drawn without replacement, what is the probability that at least one is an Ace?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Use complement: P(at least 1 Ace) = 1 - P(no Ace)
Step 2: P(no Ace) = \(\frac{48}{52} \times \frac{47}{51}\)
Step 3: P(no Ace) = \(\frac{48 \times 47}{52 \times 51} = \frac{2256}{2652} = \frac{188}{221}\)
Step 4: P(at least 1 Ace) = \(1 - \frac{188}{221} = \frac{33}{221}\)

questions.stem: Three cards are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that all three are spades?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: First spade probability = \(\frac{13}{52}\)
Step 2: Second spade probability = \(\frac{12}{51}\)
Step 3: Third spade probability = \(\frac{11}{50}\)
Step 4: Combined = \(\frac{13}{52} \times \frac{12}{51} \times \frac{11}{50} = \frac{1716}{132600} = \frac{11}{850}\)

questions.stem: A card is drawn from a deck. Given that it is a red card, what is the probability that it is a heart?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: This is conditional probability P(Heart|Red)
Step 2: Red cards = \(26\) (13 hearts + 13 diamonds)
Step 3: Hearts among red cards = \(13\)
Step 4: P(Heart|Red) = \(\frac{13}{26} = \frac{1}{2}\)

questions.stem: Two cards are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that at least one is a diamond?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Use complementary probability
Step 2: P(no diamond) = \(\frac{39}{52} \times \frac{38}{51}\)
Step 3: P(no diamond) = \(\frac{39 \times 38}{52 \times 51} = \frac{1482}{2652} = \frac{26}{51}\)
Step 4: P(at least one diamond) = \(1 - \frac{26}{51} = \frac{25}{51}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of drawing a black Ace or a red King?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Black Aces = \(2\) (Clubs and Spades)
Step 2: Red Kings = \(2\) (Hearts and Diamonds)
Step 3: These are mutually exclusive
Step 4: Total favorable = \(2 + 2 = 4\)
Step 5: Probability = \(\frac{4}{52} = \frac{1}{13}\)

questions.stem: A card is selected. What is the probability it is a court card (Jack, Queen, King) or a heart?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Court cards = \(12\)
Step 2: Hearts = \(13\)
Step 3: Heart court cards = \(3\) (overlap)
Step 4: By inclusion-exclusion: \(12 + 13 - 3 = 22\)
Step 5: Probability = \(\frac{22}{52} = \frac{11}{26}\)

questions.stem: A card is drawn from a well-shuffled deck. What is the probability that it is either a club or an even-numbered card?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Clubs = \(13\)
Step 2: Even cards (2,4,6,8,10) = \(5 \times 4 = 20\)
Step 3: Even clubs = \(5\)
Step 4: By inclusion-exclusion: \(13 + 20 - 5 = 28\)
Step 5: Probability = \(\frac{28}{52} = \frac{7}{13}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability that a card drawn from a deck has value between \(4\) and \(9\) inclusive?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Cards with values 4,5,6,7,8,9
Step 2: Number of such cards per suit = \(6\)
Step 3: Total such cards = \(6 \times 4 = 24\)
Step 4: Probability = \(\frac{24}{52} = \frac{6}{13}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of drawing a card with an odd value (considering Ace=\(1\), Jack=\(11\), King=\(13\))?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Odd valued cards: A(1), 3, 5, 7, 9, J(11), K(13)
Step 2: Queen has even value \(12\)
Step 3: Odd cards per suit = \(6\)
Step 4: Total odd cards = \(6 \times 4 = 24\)
Step 5: Probability = \(\frac{24}{52} = \frac{6}{13}\)

questions.stem: Two cards are drawn from a deck without replacement. What is the probability that both are hearts?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Probability of first heart = \(\frac{13}{52}\)
Step 2: Probability of second heart = \(\frac{12}{51}\)
Step 3: Combined probability = \(\frac{13}{52} \times \frac{12}{51} = \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{12}{51} = \frac{1}{17}\)

questions.stem: Two cards are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that the first is a club and the second is not a club?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Probability of first club = \(\frac{13}{52}\)
Step 2: After removing 1 club, remaining non-clubs = \(39\)
Step 3: Probability of second non-club = \(\frac{39}{51}\)
Step 4: Combined = \(\frac{13}{52} \times \frac{39}{51} = \frac{13 \times 39}{52 \times 51}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of drawing a prime-numbered card (\(2, 3, 5, 7\)) from a standard deck?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Prime-numbered cards: 2, 3, 5, 7
Step 2: Number per suit = \(4\)
Step 3: Total prime cards = \(4 \times 4 = 16\)
Step 4: Probability = \(\frac{16}{52} = \frac{4}{13}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability that a randomly selected card is either an Ace of Spades or any King?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Ace of Spades = \(1\)
Step 2: Any King = \(4\)
Step 3: These are mutually exclusive events
Step 4: Total favorable = \(1 + 4 = 5\)
Step 5: Probability = \(\frac{5}{52}\)

questions.stem: A card is drawn. Given it's a face card, what is the probability it's a Queen?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: This is conditional probability P(Queen|Face card)
Step 2: Total face cards = \(12\)
Step 3: Queens among face cards = \(4\)
Step 4: P(Queen|Face card) = \(\frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}\)

questions.stem: Two cards are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that they form a pair (same rank)?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: After first card, 3 cards of same rank remain out of 51
Step 2: This applies regardless of first card's rank
Step 3: Probability = \(\frac{3}{51} = \frac{1}{17}\)

questions.stem: A card is drawn and replaced, then another card is drawn. What is the probability that both cards are black?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Probability of first black card = \(\frac{26}{52} = \frac{1}{2}\)
Step 2: Since replacement, probability of second black card = \(\frac{1}{2}\)
Step 3: Combined probability = \(\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{4}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of drawing a card that is not a face card?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Total cards = \(52\)
Step 2: Face cards = \(12\)
Step 3: Non-face cards = \(52 - 12 = 40\)
Step 4: Probability = \(\frac{40}{52} = \frac{10}{13}\)

questions.stem: A card is selected randomly. What is the probability it is a \(7\) or a spade?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Number of 7s = \(4\)
Step 2: Number of spades = \(13\)
Step 3: 7 of spades = \(1\) (counted in both)
Step 4: By inclusion-exclusion: \(4 + 13 - 1 = 16\)
Step 5: Probability = \(\frac{16}{52} = \frac{4}{13}\)

questions.stem: A card is drawn and not replaced. A second card is drawn. What is the probability that both cards are of the same suit?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: After first card, 12 cards of same suit remain out of 51
Step 2: This applies regardless of first card's suit
Step 3: Probability = \(\frac{12}{51} = \frac{4}{17}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of drawing a card with value less than \(5\) (considering Ace as \(1\))?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Cards less than 5: Ace(1), 2, 3, 4
Step 2: Number of such cards per suit = \(4\)
Step 3: Total such cards = \(4 \times 4 = 16\)
Step 4: Probability = \(\frac{16}{52} = \frac{4}{13}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability that a randomly drawn card is a \(10\) or a diamond?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Number of 10s = \(4\)
Step 2: Number of diamonds = \(13\)
Step 3: 10 of diamonds = \(1\) (counted in both)
Step 4: By inclusion-exclusion: \(4 + 13 - 1 = 16\)
Step 5: Probability = \(\frac{16}{52} = \frac{4}{13}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability that a randomly drawn card is a Queen of Hearts or Queen of Spades?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Queen of Hearts = \(1\) card
Step 2: Queen of Spades = \(1\) card
Step 3: Total favorable = \(2\) cards
Step 4: Probability = \(\frac{2}{52} = \frac{1}{26}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of drawing a card from the first half of the deck (cards \(A\) through \(6\) in each suit)?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Cards A through 6 per suit = \(6\) cards
Step 2: Total such cards = \(6 \times 4 = 24\)
Step 3: Probability = \(\frac{24}{52} = \frac{6}{13}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of drawing a card that is both red and a face card?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Red face cards = face cards in hearts + face cards in diamonds
Step 2: Hearts face cards = \(3\), Diamonds face cards = \(3\)
Step 3: Total red face cards = \(3 + 3 = 6\)
Step 4: Probability = \(\frac{6}{52} = \frac{3}{26}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability that a card drawn is a multiple of \(3\) (considering only number cards \(2-10\))?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Multiples of 3 in range 2-10: 3, 6, 9
Step 2: Number of such cards per suit = \(3\)
Step 3: Total such cards = \(3 \times 4 = 12\)
Step 4: Probability = \(\frac{12}{52} = \frac{3}{13}\)

questions.stem: A card is drawn randomly. What is the probability it has the same value as a die showing \(6\)?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Die shows 6, so we need cards with value 6
Step 2: Number of 6s in deck = \(4\)
Step 3: Probability = \(\frac{4}{52} = \frac{1}{13}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of drawing two consecutive hearts when two cards are drawn without replacement?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: First heart probability = \(\frac{13}{52} = \frac{1}{4}\)
Step 2: Second heart probability = \(\frac{12}{51}\)
Step 3: Combined probability = \(\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{12}{51} = \frac{12}{204} = \frac{1}{17}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of selecting a card that when its number is doubled, gives an even result?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Any number doubled is always even
Step 2: \(2 \times \text{any number} = \text{even number}\)
Step 3: This applies to all cards regardless of value
Step 4: Probability = \(\frac{52}{52} = 1\)

questions.stem: What is the probability that a randomly drawn card is either an even-numbered card or a club?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Even cards (2,4,6,8,10) = \(5 \times 4 = 20\)
Step 2: Clubs = \(13\)
Step 3: Even clubs = \(5\)
Step 4: By inclusion-exclusion: \(20 + 13 - 5 = 28\)
Step 5: Probability = \(\frac{28}{52} = \frac{7}{13}\)

questions.stem: Three cards are drawn with replacement. What is the probability that all three are red?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Probability of red card = \(\frac{26}{52} = \frac{1}{2}\)
Step 2: With replacement, each draw is independent
Step 3: Probability of three red = \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{1}{8}\)

questions.stem: Two cards are drawn with replacement. What is the probability that the first is an Ace and the second is a King?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Probability of Ace = \(\frac{4}{52} = \frac{1}{13}\)
Step 2: Probability of King (with replacement) = \(\frac{4}{52} = \frac{1}{13}\)
Step 3: Combined probability = \(\frac{1}{13} \times \frac{1}{13} = \frac{1}{169}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of drawing a numbered card (\(2\) to \(10\)) from a standard deck?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Numbered cards per suit = \(9\) (2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10)
Step 2: Total numbered cards = \(9 \times 4 = 36\)
Step 3: Probability = \(\frac{36}{52} = \frac{9}{13}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of drawing an Ace or a King from a standard deck?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Number of Aces = \(4\)
Step 2: Number of Kings = \(4\)
Step 3: Total favorable outcomes = \(4 + 4 = 8\)
Step 4: Probability = \(\frac{8}{52} = \frac{2}{13}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of drawing a Jack of Hearts or any Queen?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Jack of Hearts = \(1\)
Step 2: Any Queen = \(4\)
Step 3: These are mutually exclusive
Step 4: Total favorable = \(1 + 4 = 5\)
Step 5: Probability = \(\frac{5}{52}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of drawing a card that is a spade but not a face card?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Total spades = \(13\)
Step 2: Spade face cards = \(3\) (Jack, Queen, King of spades)
Step 3: Non-face spades = \(13 - 3 = 10\)
Step 4: Probability = \(\frac{10}{52} = \frac{5}{26}\)

questions.stem: A card is drawn from a deck of \(52\) cards. What is the probability that it is a red card?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Total cards = \(52\)
Step 2: Red cards (Hearts + Diamonds) = \(26\)
Step 3: Probability = \(\frac{26}{52} = \frac{1}{2}\)

questions.stem: Two cards are drawn with replacement. What is the probability that exactly one is black?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: P(black) = \(\frac{1}{2}\), P(red) = \(\frac{1}{2}\)
Step 2: Exactly one black = (Black,Red) OR (Red,Black)
Step 3: P(B,R) = \(\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{4}\)
Step 4: P(R,B) = \(\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{4}\)
Step 5: Total = \(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{2}\)

questions.stem: A card is drawn from a deck. What is the probability that it is a heart given that it is red?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: This is P(Heart|Red)
Step 2: Red cards = \(26\) (13 hearts + 13 diamonds)
Step 3: Hearts among red = \(13\)
Step 4: P(Heart|Red) = \(\frac{13}{26} = \frac{1}{2}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of drawing a King from a standard deck of \(52\) cards?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Total number of cards = \(52\)
Step 2: Number of Kings in a deck = \(4\)
Step 3: Probability = \(\frac{4}{52} = \frac{1}{13}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of drawing either a diamond or a black card?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Diamonds = \(13\)
Step 2: Black cards = \(26\)
Step 3: These events are mutually exclusive
Step 4: Total favorable = \(13 + 26 = 39\)
Step 5: Probability = \(\frac{39}{52} = \frac{3}{4}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability of drawing a face card (Jack, Queen, King) from a standard deck?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Face cards per suit = \(3\) (Jack, Queen, King)
Step 2: Total face cards = \(3 \times 4 = 12\)
Step 3: Probability = \(\frac{12}{52} = \frac{3}{13}\)

questions.stem: What is the probability that a card drawn is a picture card (Jack, Queen, King) and is red?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Picture cards = Jack, Queen, King
Step 2: Red picture cards = \(3\) from hearts + \(3\) from diamonds = \(6\)
Step 3: Probability = \(\frac{6}{52} = \frac{3}{26}\)
